I've been working this land for 30 years, same county, same soil. I know what works here and what doesn't. My 3 mu splits like this: 2 mu stays in wheat-maize rotation the way it always has, and 1 mu I keep in cotton. Cotton is more work, but my wife and I can handle 1 mu of it, and the cash price is still worth it for me. My son is off-farm now, so I can't take on more labor than that.

**Wheat (winter, 2 mu):** I'll use the improved variety I've been buying from the county seed store — same one as last few years, yields fine. I rotary-till after the maize harvest in September, apply compound fertilizer as base, then push urea in February when jointing starts. I water three times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. Two rounds of spraying — herbicide in late autumn, then something for aphids and powdery mildew in spring. Should get around 430 jin per mu.

**Maize (summer, 2 mu):** Right after I cut the wheat in June, I direct-seed maize into the stubble. No-till saves me time and diesel. Hybrid seed, the kind everyone around here uses. I put compound fertilizer in the seed furrow and topdress urea when the maize is knee-high. Two waterings unless it rains enough. One herbicide pass early, one spray if I see corn borers.

**Cotton (1 mu, spring):** Plant in late April after soil warms. Hybrid cotton. This one takes the most spraying — aphids, bollworms, spider mites. Four applications is normal, sometimes five if it's a bad year. Three waterings. Rotary-till in spring to prepare the bed.
